sources.title: M. M. Cohen, A Course in Simple-Homotopy Theory (Springer GTM 10, university-hosted full scan)
sources.locator: Chapter I §§7.3–7.4 pp.25–27 and §§8.1–8.6 pp.28–33; Chapter III §§19–23 pp.62–77 (printed pages; scanned two-up PDF)
sources.reading_verification: Downloaded full 64-page scanned two-up PDF on 2026-09-24; rendered and visually read printed pp.24–33 and 62–77, including complete proofs of §§7.3–7.4, 8.1–8.5, 19–23. Section 8.6 on p.33 was inspected for its unit example. The design’s Chapters 1–7 locator alone does not reach algebraic torsion or the hard converse.

contents.name: §7.2 Finite simplicial models of finite CW complexes
contents.reason: Finite simplicial triangulation up to simple type is a separate approximation theorem; the assigned torsion obstruction is constructed directly for finite CW complexes and never uses this model.

contents.name: §7.3 Trading cells
contents.support: Explicit elementary expansion followed by collapse trades a lowest relative r-cell for a higher cell when π_r(K,L)=0.

contents.name: §7.4 Simplified form
contents.support: Repeated finite trading gives a simple equivalent pair with relative cells in two adjacent degrees; choose the lower degree at least three.

contents.name: §8.1 Relative homotopy as a free group-ring module
contents.support: For degree at least three the relative homotopy of a single cell layer is free over the fundamental group ring with the characteristic-cell basis; degree two needs an extra constant-attachment condition.

contents.name: §8.2 Identity-matrix cell cancellation
contents.support: Use the relative homotopy basis, a homotopy of characteristic maps and HEP to turn identity incidence into genuine elementary collapses.

contents.name: §§8.3–8.4 Row, column, unit and stabilization moves
contents.support: Geometric changes of attaching maps and elementary pairs realize stable elementary operations and trivial units, reducing zero torsion matrices to the identity.

contents.name: §8.5 Vanishing torsion and simple type
contents.support: Proves the relative converse by simplified form, elementary matrix moves and identity-matrix cancellation.

contents.name: §8.6 Nontrivial units in Z[C5]
contents.support: The unit 1−t+t² has a nontrivial determinant class; the manifest uses the independently checked 1−t²−t³ unit from Lurie instead.

contents.name: §19 Torsion of a CW pair
contents.support: Defines relative torsion and proves independence of lifts, orientations and basepoint up to the correct Whitehead quotient.

contents.name: §§20–21 Sum, excision and natural equivalence
contents.support: Cellular pair additivity and naturality supply the typed based-pair sum formula.

contents.name: §22 Torsion of a homotopy equivalence
contents.support: Mapping-cylinder definition, homotopy invariance and τ(gf)=τ(g)+g_*τ(f).

contents.name: §23 Sum theorem
contents.support: Gives the pushout sum relation after transporting torsion to the common target group ring.

sources.title: Wolfgang Lück, A Basic Introduction to Surgery Theory (full lecture-note monograph)
sources.locator: Chapter 2 §§2.1–2.3, printed pp.24–38, especially Lemmas 2.2, 2.9, 2.18–2.20 and Theorem 2.21
sources.reading_verification: Downloaded and extracted full 197-page PDF on 2026-09-24; read printed pp.24–38 continuously. The proof of Theorem 2.21 injectivity is explicitly a sketch referring to Cohen pp.25–26 and Chapter II §8; Cohen was checked directly.

contents.name: §2.1 Whitehead groups and Lemma 2.2
contents.support: Elementary matrices generate the stable commutator subgroup, establishing abelian K1 and Wh(G).

contents.name: Lemma 2.4, matrix-operation quotient agrees with Wh(G)
contents.support: Normality of E(R) identifies the elementary-matrix equivalence relation with the abelian Whitehead quotient used in the definition.

contents.name: Remark 2.5, projective-module presentation of K1
contents.reason: The projective-module presentation is equivalent but needs additional projective-module theory; finite free right modules and stable matrices suffice for every assigned Whitehead torsion claim.

contents.name: Definition 2.6 and equation (2.7), contraction torsion
contents.support: Uses d+γ from odd to even and reduced K1; triangular comparison removes the contraction choice.

contents.name: Lemma 2.9, exact sum, homotopy invariance and composition
contents.support: Based exact cone sequence, triangular basis changes, chain homotopy invariance and composition.

contents.name: Definition 2.13, torsion on finite CW complexes
contents.support: Defines torsion in the target Whitehead group and handles basepoint transport and disconnected spaces componentwise.

contents.name: Theorem 2.1, topological properties of torsion
contents.locator: p.32 (algebraic properties; theorem statement extends onto p.23)
contents.support: Choice independence and naturality; the manifold/homeomorphism clause is disposed separately.

contents.name: Theorem 2.1(5), Chapman homeomorphism invariance
contents.locator: p.32 (proof reference only; deep clause not used)
contents.reason: The Chapman theorem is a deep theorem about arbitrary homeomorphisms and is outside the assigned finite CW cellular simple-homotopy construction; it is not used in any proof here.

contents.name: Theorem 2.1(4), product formula for torsion
contents.reason: The product formula is a separate application beyond the required composition and based-pair sum formulas; no item in this assigned pair uses it or claims product torsion.

contents.name: Lemma 2.16, h-cobordism gluing and duality
contents.reason: The smooth h-cobordism and Poincaré duality applications belong to later DT-24 and manifold theory, not this AT-owned algebraic simple-homotopy page.

contents.name: Definition 2.17, elementary expansions and collapses
contents.support: Attaches a cell pair with a free face and defines simple homotopy equivalence through finite elementary moves.

contents.name: Lemma 2.18(1), elementary expansion has zero torsion
contents.support: Relative universal-cover chains are a two-term identity complex.

contents.name: Lemma 2.18(2), realization of every Whitehead class
contents.support: Attach high-dimensional spheres and upper cells with an invertible group-ring boundary matrix.

contents.name: Lemmas 2.19–2.20, mapping cylinder expansion
contents.support: Each target-cylinder cell contributes an explicit elementary pair; relative inclusion reduction follows.

contents.name: Theorem 2.21, geometric Whitehead obstruction
contents.support: States the exact converse and sketches the cell-trading, matrix-move and cancellation proof completed by Cohen.

sources.title: James F. Davis and Paul Kirk, Lecture Notes in Algebraic Topology (complete book-length notes)
sources.locator: Chapter 11 §11.4, printed pp.343–345; Theorem 11.31 and its full proofs of parts (1)–(2), converse sketch
sources.reading_verification: Downloaded full 382-page author-hosted PDF and extracted text on 2026-09-24; read §11.4 continuously. The authors explicitly label converse only a sketch and refer to Cohen §§7.3, 8.2–8.3.

contents.name: §11.4 Universal-cover based cellular chains
contents.support: One oriented lift per cell gives a finite free group-ring basis.

contents.name: Theorem 11.31(1), torsion independence
contents.support: Explains orientation, deck lift, basepoint and cellular approximation invariance.

contents.name: Theorem 11.31(2), simple implies zero
contents.support: Computes elementary expansion and collapse torsion using a relative two-term complex.

contents.name: Theorem 11.31(3), zero torsion implies simple
contents.support: Sketches cell-trading, cell sliding and cell cancellation; Cohen supplies the full geometry.

contents.name: Theorem 11.32, Chapman homeomorphism theorem
contents.reason: The deep homeomorphism invariance theorem goes beyond the assigned finite cellular maps and is not needed for the algebraic torsion obstruction or examples.

sources.title: Andrew Casson, Simple Homotopy Theory (university-hosted full notes)
sources.locator: Chapter 4, Theorem 4.7 and its proof, PDF printed pp.32–34
sources.reading_verification: Downloaded full 47-page author-hosted PDF and extracted text on 2026-09-24; read the complete Theorem 4.7 proof, with scanned typographical errors cross-checked against Cohen and Lück.

contents.name: Theorem 4.7, zero Whitehead torsion characterizes simple homotopy
contents.support: Independent full geometric argument: cell trading, elementary matrix changes and cancellation.

sources.title: Jacob Lurie, Whitehead Torsion, Part II (Lecture 4)
sources.locator: Lecture 4, pp.1–4, Propositions 1 and 4, Lemma 2, Corollary 5, Remark 6, Examples 7 and 9, Theorem 8 and proof sketch
sources.reading_verification: Downloaded and extracted the complete four-page lecture on 2026-09-24. The Example 11 cell-attachment claim omits the needed assumption that the two attaching maps are homotopic; the manifest states that hypothesis explicitly.

contents.name: Proposition 1, homotopy invariance
contents.support: Cellular homotopic maps have equal torsion by the cylinder and composition formula.

contents.name: Lemma 2 and Proposition 4, composition
contents.support: Based cone extensions give the composition identity; manifest uses additive notation and target transport.

contents.name: Corollary 5, elementary expansion
contents.support: Relative two-term boundary is a trivial group unit.

contents.name: Remark 6, realization of Whitehead classes
contents.support: Attaches high sphere cells and upper cells realizing an invertible matrix.

contents.name: Example 7, nontrivial Whitehead class for C5
contents.support: The unit 1−t²−t³ with inverse 1−t−t⁴ is not ±t^k; determinant detects its class.

contents.name: Theorem 8, zero torsion converse
contents.support: Independent proof outline using mapping cylinder, high two-layer normal form and elementary matrix moves; Cohen gives detailed geometry.

contents.name: Example 9, Wh(1)=0
contents.support: K1(Z) reduces to determinant ±1, both killed in Wh(1).

contents.name: Example 10, Wh(Z^d)=0 and s-cobordism application
contents.reason: Bass–Heller–Swan and smooth s-cobordism are separate deep results outside this assigned finite CW obstruction page; neither is used as a dependency.

contents.name: Example 11, homotopic attaching maps
contents.support: Use only with the mathematically necessary explicit hypothesis that the two attaching maps are homotopic; the source statement omits it.

contents.name: Remark 12, Whitehead matrix lemma
contents.support: Stable commutator matrices factor into elementary block shears.

dependency_audit: Finite CW and group-ring proof routes checked; precise item-level dependency evidence is in the Step 1 records and batch notes.
